instantiated_cells.justification: Principals registered under § 13.64 must file expense statements on or before July 31 and January 31, not annually.
The statute sets semiannual deadlines (Jan. 31 and July 31) for principal expense statements, not monthly reporting.
The only periodic filing schedule specified for principal expense statements is twice yearly (Jan. 31 and July 31), so no other frequency option applies.
Principal expense statements are due January 31 and July 31, not quarterly.
Registered principals must file an expense statement on or before July 31 and January 31 covering each preceding 6-month reporting period.
Reporting periods are defined as 6-month periods and statements are filed twice yearly, not on a tri-annual legislative-calendar basis.
Principal registration requires describing the business activity or the principal’s nature and purposes, thereby disclosing the nature of the business/organization.
The expense statement must include lobbying expenditures including compensation to lobbyists for lobbying (cash or in-kind) and reimbursements.
Principals must disclose time spent meeting with officials, but the statute does not require reporting the identities of contacts/individuals contacted as lobbying contacts.
Principals must report each legislative proposal/rule/budget subject or, if none, each lobbying topic with reasonable specificity and also estimate time by proposal/topic in the expense statement.
The principal expense statement must list any official/candidate to whom the principal or its lobbyist provided reimbursement authorized under § 13.621(7)(a), including date and amount.

The expense statement includes non-compensation lobbying costs such as research/analysis, paid advertising to urge public lobbying, office overhead for in-house lobbyists, and travel and living expenses.
If amounts to any lobbyist exceed $200 in the reporting period, the principal must list the lobbyist’s name and address and total amount paid/incurred.
The expense statement requires listing a lobbyist’s name and address only when expenditures/obligations to that lobbyist exceed $200 during the reporting period, not all lobbyists in every case.
The bundled provisions specify reporting of lobbying expenditures, time, topics, and lobbyist payments but do not require disclosure of the principal’s major financial contributors.

Registration requires the principal’s name and business address, but the statute does not require a principal telephone number (telephone is only mentioned for the optional verified statement under § 13.621(5)).

Principals must report each 'legislative proposal' in connection with which they have made or intend to make a lobbying communication, which identifies the specific proposal (bill) rather than only general issues.

The statement must report the aggregate total amount of lobbying expenditures made and obligations incurred for lobbying by the principal and all lobbyists for the principal (subject to listed exclusions).

The expense statement includes compensation to lobbyists and, if totals to any lobbyist exceed $200 in the period, requires reporting the total amount paid/incurred to that lobbyist along with name and address.
The required time record must include a daily itemization of time spent lobbying-related activities, which is an itemized (not solely lump-sum) reporting format.
Associations must report the chief executive officer and approximate number of members, but the statute does not require listing the names of all members/sponsors.

When payments/obligations to a lobbyist exceed $200 in a reporting period, the principal must list that lobbyist by name and address, providing an explicit lobbyist-listing requirement in spending reports.
